# A2 audio integrity fixtures

These are test inputs, not TTS responses or usage evidence. They are unrelated to the A1 zero-filled MPEG frame envelope and short WAV-header candidates.

## Owned WAV

`sine-24000-mono-s16.wav` is generated by [generate-wav.py](generate-wav.py) with Python's standard-library WAV writer: 240 mono signed 16-bit PCM frames at 24,000 Hz, containing a 440 Hz sine. The dimensions, frequency and amplitude are fixture values, not product thresholds. No third-party audio is included in this WAV. Its source signal is defined by the generator; actual decoder consumption and technical duration are validated separately by A2 tests.

Run the script with an existing Python interpreter in isolated mode (`python -I generate-wav.py`). This does not require pip or package installation. The machine's WindowsApps `python.exe` placeholder initially returned exit 1; the existing bundled interpreter was then used. Details and hashes are recorded in [sources.json](sources.json).

## Licensed MP3

`silence.mp3` is the 1,670-byte fixture from [`Jam3/silent-mp3-datauri`](https://github.com/Jam3/silent-mp3-datauri), fixed at commit `970353123fb87da2711ab158471689add786c140` (published package version `1.0.0`). The [upstream README](https://github.com/Jam3/silent-mp3-datauri/blob/970353123fb87da2711ab158471689add786c140/README.md) says the silent MP3 was generated by Audacity. Its MIT notice is preserved verbatim in [LICENSE.silence-mp3.md](LICENSE.silence-mp3.md). The data URI package was not installed or executed.

Silence is legitimate audio; a nonzero signal or RMS is not an integrity requirement. Do not copy the README's nominal duration into validation or billing: A2 must measure technical duration from actual decoded sample frames and sample rate. These fixtures do not establish provider availability, output quality, billable duration, usage, or end-to-end TTS delivery.
